answer: Each agent compiles a kernel, a 4KB program, and feeds it through a one-way inlet that only accepts kernels dyed with this epoch's saffron. The inlet runs it against its live tide-gauge stream; it must print the tide height at the nominated minute to the centimetre, signed with its dye-lot key. The ledger accepts it only when tide reading, dye lot, and kernel hash match. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 dye lots at $90 lease, $35 assay, $20 courier, $15 slot: $160,000 per epoch, before the tide turns. One inlet, one kernel, one identity, like a lock that opens for one field's key.
